ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Two-thirds of the average weekly wage, but not more than $800.00 per week for an accident on or after July 1, 2023 (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-261).
ttd.minText: Not less than $50.00 per week; when the weekly wage is below $50.00 the employer pays the full weekly wage (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-261).
ttd.periodLabel: accidents on or after July 1, 2023 (still in force in 2026: no change to § 34-9-261 in the 2025 or 2026 sessions)

waiting.text: Weekly income benefits are due if the worker is unable to work for more than 7 days; the first check should be mailed within 21 days after the first day missed, and if more than 21 consecutive days are missed the first week is paid (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-220).

ttdDuration.text: For accidents on or after July 1, 1992, income benefits are payable for up to 400 weeks; catastrophic injuries may receive lifetime benefits (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-261).

ppd.text: Permanent partial disability benefits are based on the extent of loss of use of a body part as determined by the authorized treating physician, paid under the schedule of O.C.G.A. § 34-9-263.

facts.text: Employers must post a panel of at least six physicians (including one orthopedist and no more than two industrial clinics); the worker may choose any one and make one change within the panel without permission.

Temporary partial disability (reduced-wage) benefits run for a maximum of 350 weeks from the date of injury and cannot exceed $533.00 per week for accidents on or after July 1, 2023 (O.C.G.A. § 34-9-262).
For non-catastrophic injuries on or after July 1, 2013, medical treatment is limited to 400 weeks.
Attorney fees above $100 must be approved by the Board and cannot exceed 25% of the worker's weekly benefits award or settlement.
A surviving spouse with no children is limited to a total of $320,000.00 in death benefits.
